children: , a leader in end-to-end supply chain solutions for the transportation, logistics and infrastructure markets, will showcase application-specific tank trailer solutions, safety technology and lifecycle support at National Tank Truck Carriers’ 2026 Tank Truck Week, Sept. 27-30 in Oklahoma City.

At booth #1239, Wabash will display three tank trailers, including a specialty chemical trailer, fleet chemical trailer and frame-and-cradle sanitary trailer, while highlighting valve technology from Betts Industries. The exhibit brings Wabash’s “Built Around Your Business” approach to life through application-specific engineering, configurations tailored to each operation and practical tank expertise designed to help customers address critical priorities: safety, uptime and payload.

“Safety is always at the forefront in tank transportation, but our customers are also balancing uptime, payload and the specific requirements of the products they haul,” said Adam Quinn, senior director of tank trailer sales at Wabash. “That’s why we take an application-focused approach to tank design. Whether it’s helping a food-grade hauler maximize payload while protecting product integrity or designing a chemical trailer for durability and efficient unloading, the goal is to give customers equipment that performs for the realities of their business.”

“Wabash has consistently supported us in both winning and retaining customers because they take the time to understand what each operation needs,” said Brian O’Donnell, president of Stuart Tank. “We’ve worked together to design trailers that optimize weight and maximize payload while maintaining the durability our customers expect, as well as configurations that prioritize driver safety and ergonomics. Most importantly, Wabash listens. When a customer has unique requirements, they’re willing to work alongside us to understand the operation firsthand and develop a solution around those specific needs.”
The Original Frame & Cradle Tank Trailer

Wabash has been building its frame-and-cradle tank design for more than 50 years, drawing on decades of real-world use and customer input to continually refine the design for today's sanitary hauling applications. Its unique aluminum frame-and-cradle design is approximately 250 to 500 pounds lighter than traditional stainless-steel designs, helping maximize payload. Tension-fit rings support a smooth internal barrel finish and more consistent insulation coverage helps keep food-grade products colder for longer in transit.

Wabash supports liquid-transport applications including chemical, sanitary, food-grade, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and corrosives/FRP. Customers can select application-based packages or work directly with Wabash engineering teams to customize material grades, insulation, pumps, meters, integrated safety systems and other specifications based on operating requirements.

The Wabash FRP tank uses automated winding technology to create a one-piece barrel that reduces seams and potential weak points while providing a lightweight, corrosion-resistant alternative to stainless steel. Chemical tanks incorporate wide stainless-steel sheets, precision welding, 2205 duplex stainless heat panels and an integrated outlet sump designed for complete drainage. Acutherm™ Sanitary tanks use a lightweight frame-and-cradle, tension-fit ring construction designed to support durability, payload efficiency and product integrity.
Advancing Tank Safety and Product Integrity

Wabash will also highlight valve technology from Betts Industries designed to provide greater visibility into the status of valves, vents and manhole openings and closings. The technology can help operators verify that outlets are properly closed, helping reduce opportunities for product contamination while reducing the need for drivers to climb on top of tanks to inspect seals.
Lifecycle Support That Protects Uptime and Value

Wabash helps customers maximize uptime throughout the equipment lifecycle with dedicated parts, service and technical expertise. Five tank trailer parts and service locations in Ashland, KY; Baton Rouge, LA; Houston, Texas; Mauston, WI; and Memphis, TN provide repair, inspection, modifications and other lifecycle support.
These capabilities build on Wabash’s deep tank industry experience and bring the heritage of its tank brands together within a broader tank portfolio.
Wabash representatives will be available throughout Tank Truck Week to discuss application requirements, trailer specifications, safety technology and lifecycle support.
